questions.knowledge_point: Integrating a Rational Function With an Irreducible Trinomial Quadratic Factor
questions.worked_solution:
Notice that the quadratic factor in the denominator has a negative discriminant:

$$
D=(-2)^{2}-4(1)(3)=-8<0
$$

So, we proceed with the following partial fraction decomposition:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{x}^{2}+x-3}{({x}^{2}-2x+3)(x+1)} & =\frac{Ax+B}{{x}^{2}-2x+3}+\frac{C}{x+1}\end{aligned}
$$

To determine the coefficients $A,$ $B,$ and $C,$ we first multiply both sides of the above equation by $({x}^{2}-2x+3)(x+1)$ and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+x-3 & =(Ax+B)(x+1)+C({x}^{2}-2x+3).\end{aligned}
$$

Solving for the unknown constants using the usual methods, we get  $A=\frac{3}{2},$ $B=-\frac{3}{2},$ and $C=-\frac{1}{2}.$ Therefore,

$$
\frac{{x}^{2}+x-3}{({x}^{2}-2x+3)(x+1)}=\frac{3x-3}{2({x}^{2}-2x+3)}-\frac{1}{2(x+1)}.
$$

Now we integrate this function term by term, adding the constant of integration only at the very end.

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{{x}^{2}+x-3}{({x}^{2}-2x+3)(x+1)}\,\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{3x-3}{2({x}^{2}-2x+3)}-\frac{1}{2(x+1)})\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{3}{2}\int \frac{x-1}{{x}^{2}-2x+3}\,\text{d}x-\frac{1}{2}\int \frac{1}{x+1}\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

For the first integral, we use the substitution $u={x}^{2}-2x+3.$ Then $(2x-2)\,\text{d}x=\text{d}u,$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{x-1}{{x}^{2}-2x+3}\,\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{1}{u})\frac{\text{d}u}{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡|u| \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡|{x}^{2}-2x+3| \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}-2x+3).\end{aligned}
$$

For the second integral we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{1}{x+1}\,\text{d}x & =\operatorname{ln}⁡|x+1|.\end{aligned}
$$

So we get the following result:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{{x}^{2}+x-3}{({x}^{2}-2x+3)(x+1)}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{3}{2}\int \frac{x-1}{{x}^{2}-2x+3}\,\text{d}x-\frac{1}{2}\int \frac{1}{x+1}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{3}{2}\cdot \frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}-2x+3)-\frac{1}{2}\cdot \operatorname{ln}⁡|x+1|+K \\  & =\frac{3}{4}\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}-2x+3)-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡|x+1|+K.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Integrating a Rational Function With an Irreducible Binomial Quadratic Factor
questions.worked_solution:
The quadratic factor ${x}^{2}+7$ is irreducible, so we proceed with the following partial fraction decomposition:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{x}^{2}+2x+17}{({x}^{2}+7)(x+1)} & =\frac{Ax+B}{{x}^{2}+7}+\frac{C}{x+1}\end{aligned}
$$

To determine the coefficients $A,B,$ and $C,$ we first multiply both sides of the above equation by $({x}^{2}+7)(x+1),$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+2x+17 & =(Ax+B)(x+1)+C({x}^{2}+7).\end{aligned}
$$

Solving for the unknown constants using the usual methods, we get $A=-1,B=3,$ and $C=2.$ Therefore,

$$
\frac{{x}^{2}+2x+17}{({x}^{2}+7)(x+1)}=\frac{-x+3}{{x}^{2}+7}+\frac{2}{x+1}.
$$

We now integrate this function term by term, adding the constant of integration at the very end.

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{{x}^{2}+2x+17}{({x}^{2}+7)(x+1)}\,\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{-x+3}{{x}^{2}+7}+\frac{2}{x+1})\text{d}x \\  & =-\int \frac{x}{{x}^{2}+7}\,\text{d}x+3\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+7}\,\text{d}x+2\int \frac{1}{x+1}\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

For the first integral, we use a substitution $u={x}^{2}+7.$ Then $\text{d}u=2x\,\text{d}x,$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{x}{{x}^{2}+7}\,\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{1}{u})\frac{\text{d}u}{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡|u| \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡|{x}^{2}+7| \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+7).\end{aligned}
$$

For the second integral, we use the fact that $\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+{a}^{2}}\,\text{d}x=\frac{1}{a}\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{x}{a}),$ which results in

$$
\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+7}\,\text{d}x=\frac{1}{\sqrt{7}}\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{x}{\sqrt{7}}).
$$

Finally, for the third integral, we have

$$
\int \frac{1}{x+1}\,\text{d}x=\operatorname{ln}⁡|x+1|.
$$

So, we get the following result:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{{x}^{2}+2x+17}{({x}^{2}+7)(x+1)}\,\text{d}x & =-\int \frac{x}{{x}^{2}+7}\,\text{d}x+3\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+7}\,\text{d}x+2\int \frac{1}{x+1}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+7)+3\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{7}}\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{x}{\sqrt{7}})+2\cdot \operatorname{ln}⁡|x+1|+K \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+7)+\frac{3}{\sqrt{7}}\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{x}{\sqrt{7}})+2\operatorname{ln}⁡|x+1|+K\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Integrating a Rational Function With an Irreducible Trinomial Quadratic Factor
questions.worked_solution:
Notice that the quadratic factor in the denominator has a discriminant that is not a perfect square:

$$
D=(-4)^{2}-4(1)(-3)=28
$$

We have that $\sqrt{28}$ is not a rational number, which implies that the quadratic factor doesn't factor over the rational numbers.

So, we proceed with the following partial fraction decomposition:

$$
\frac{2{x}^{2}-3x-9}{(x+3)({x}^{2}-4x-3)}=\frac{A}{x+3}+\frac{Bx+C}{{x}^{2}-4x-3}
$$

To determine the coefficients $A,B,$ and $C,$ we first multiply both sides of the above equation by $(x+3)({x}^{2}-4x-3),$ and we get

$$
2{x}^{2}-3x-9=A({x}^{2}-4x-3)+(Bx+C)(x+3)
$$

Solving for the unknown constants using the usual methods, we get $A=1,B=1$ and $C=-2.$ Therefore,

$$
\frac{2{x}^{2}-3x-9}{(x+3)({x}^{2}-4x-3)}=\frac{1}{x+3}+\frac{x-2}{{x}^{2}-4x-3}.
$$

We now integrate this function term by term, adding the constant of integration at the very end.

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{2{x}^{2}-3x-9}{(x+3)({x}^{2}-4x-3)}\,\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{1}{x+3}+\frac{x-2}{{x}^{2}-4x-3})\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int \frac{1}{x+3}\,\text{d}x+\int \frac{x-2}{{x}^{2}-4x-3}\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

For the first integral, we have

$$
\int \frac{1}{x+3}\,\text{d}x=\operatorname{ln}⁡|x+3|.
$$

For the second integral, we use the substitution $u={x}^{2}-4x-3.$ Then $\text{d}u=2(x-2)\,\text{d}x,$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{x-2}{{x}^{2}-4x-3}\,\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{1}{u})\frac{\text{d}u}{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡|u| \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡|{x}^{2}-4x-3|\end{aligned}
$$

So, we get the following result:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{2{x}^{2}-3x-9}{(x+3)({x}^{2}-4x-3)}\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{1}{x+3}\,\text{d}x+\int \frac{x-2}{{x}^{2}-4x-3}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡|x+3|+\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡|{x}^{2}-4x-3|+K.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Integrating a Rational Function With an Irreducible Binomial Quadratic Factor
questions.worked_solution:
The quadratic factor ${x}^{2}+1$ is irreducible, so we proceed with the following partial fraction decomposition:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{3{x}^{2}-9x+5}{({x}^{2}+1)(x-4)} & =\frac{Ax+B}{{x}^{2}+1}+\frac{C}{x-4}\end{aligned}
$$

To determine the coefficients $A,B,$ and $C,$ we first multiply both sides of the above equation by $({x}^{2}+1)(x-4),$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}3{x}^{2}-9x+5 & =(Ax+B)(x-4)+C({x}^{2}+1).\end{aligned}
$$

Solving for the unknown constants using the usual methods, we get $A=2,B=-1,$ and $C=1.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{3{x}^{2}-9x+5}{({x}^{2}+1)(x-4)} & =\frac{2x-1}{{x}^{2}+1}+\frac{1}{x-4}\end{aligned}
$$

We now integrate this function term by term, adding the constant of integration at the very end.

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{3{x}^{2}-9x+5}{({x}^{2}+1)(x-4)}\,\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{2x-1}{{x}^{2}+1}+\frac{1}{x-4})\text{d}x \\  & =\int \frac{2x}{{x}^{2}+1}\,\text{d}x-\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+1}\,\text{d}x+\int \frac{1}{x-4}\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

For the first integral, we use the substitution $u={x}^{2}+3.$ Then $\text{d}u=2x\,\text{d}x,$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{2x}{{x}^{2}+1}\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{1}{u}\text{d}u \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡|u| \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡|{x}^{2}+1| \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+1).\end{aligned}
$$

For the second integral, we use the fact that $\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+{a}^{2}}\,\text{d}x=\frac{1}{a}\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{x}{a}),$ which results in

$$
\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+1}\,\text{d}x=\operatorname{arctan}⁡(x).
$$

Finally, for the third integral, we have

$$
\int \frac{1}{x-4}\,\text{d}x=\operatorname{ln}⁡|x-4|.
$$

So, we get the following result:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{3{x}^{2}-9x+5}{({x}^{2}+1)(x-4)}\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{2x}{{x}^{2}+1}\,\text{d}x-\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+1}\,\text{d}x+\int \frac{1}{x-4}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+1)-\operatorname{arctan}⁡(x)+\operatorname{ln}⁡|x-4|+K\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Integrating a Rational Function With an Irreducible Trinomial Quadratic Factor
questions.worked_solution:
Notice that the quadratic factor in the denominator has a discriminant that is not a perfect square:

$$
D=(4)^{2}-4(1)(-6)=40
$$

We have that $\sqrt{40}$ is not a rational number, which implies that the quadratic factor doesn't factor over the rational numbers.

So, we proceed with the following partial fraction decomposition:

$$
\frac{4{x}^{2}+12x-12}{x({x}^{2}+4x-6)}=\frac{A}{x}+\frac{Bx+C}{{x}^{2}+4x-6}
$$

To determine the coefficients $A,B,$ and $C,$ we first multiply both sides of the above equation by $x({x}^{2}+4x-6),$ and we get

$$
4{x}^{2}+12x-12=A({x}^{2}+4x-6)+(Bx+C)x
$$

Solving for the unknown constants using the usual methods, we get $A=2,B=2$, and $C=4.$ Therefore,

$$
\frac{4{x}^{2}+12x-12}{x({x}^{2}+4x-6)}=\frac{2}{x}+\frac{2x+4}{{x}^{2}+4x-6}.
$$

We now integrate this function term by term, adding the constant of integration at the very end.

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{4{x}^{2}+12x-12}{x({x}^{2}+4x-6)}\,\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{2}{x}+\frac{2x+4}{{x}^{2}+4x-6})\,\text{d}x \\  & =2\int \frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x+\int \frac{2x+4}{{x}^{2}+4x-6}\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

For the first integral, we have

$$
\int \frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x=\operatorname{ln}⁡|x|.
$$

For the second integral, we use the substitution $u={x}^{2}+4x-6.$ Then $\text{d}u=(2x+4)\,\text{d}x,$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{2x+4}{{x}^{2}+4x-6}\,\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{1}{u})\text{d}u \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡|u| \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡|{x}^{2}+4x-6|\end{aligned}
$$

So, we get the following result:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{4{x}^{2}+12x-12}{x({x}^{2}+4x-6)}\,\text{d}x & =2\int \frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x+\int \frac{2x+4}{{x}^{2}+4x-6}\,\text{d}x \\  & =2\operatorname{ln}⁡|x|+\operatorname{ln}⁡|{x}^{2}+4x-6|+K.\end{aligned}
$$
